cards.title: Two things, not four boxes
cards.body: Home feels like a mix of warmth and expectations. The four named styles are corners of that map, not types of person. Most days you move around it.

cards.title: Warm and clear
cards.body: Children tend to do well on school, mood and friendships when warmth and clear limits go together. This is a link in studies, not a promise, and it is not risk-free.

cards.title: Climate and tools
cards.body: Style is the emotional climate. Practices are the tools. The same tool, such as a time-out, lands differently in a warm home than in a cold one.

cards.title: Children shape parents too
cards.body: Twin studies estimate that about a quarter of the variation in parenting is driven by the child. Parent and child influence each other, so nobody is to blame for the whole picture.

cards.title: Culture changes the meaning
cards.body: A firm, high-expectation style can mean care and training in some families and coldness in others. Research found the same style linked to opposite school results in different communities.

cards.title: Gentle means kind and firm
cards.body: Gentle parenting has no studies of its own. Its ingredients, warmth, validation and limits that are held, match research on authoritative parenting. The risk is dropping the limits. Check: did I say the limit, and did I hold it?

cards.title: A short, calm time-out
cards.body: Name what happened, use a boring safe spot, stay calm and quiet, then reconnect. About one minute per year of age. Skip long isolation and punishing tears.

cards.title: Hitting does not teach
cards.body: Pediatric guidance advises against physical punishment. It is less effective than time-outs or losing a privilege and is linked to more defiance.

cards.title: Specific praise
cards.body: Name the thing they did. "You shared the red block" lands better than "good boy".

cards.title: Say it plainly
cards.body: If it is an instruction, say it as one, once, in specific words. "Shoes on, please" works better than "Can you put your shoes on?"

cards.title: Naming feelings
cards.body: Emotion coaching reliably changes what parents do. Evidence that it improves 5 to 7 year olds' emotion skills is still thin and mostly parent-reported.

cards.title: How you disagree matters most
cards.body: Hostility and withdrawal between parents are linked to more child problems because a child may feel the family is unsafe. Calm disagreement that gets resolved is not harmful.

cards.title: Keep your child out of the middle
cards.body: No messengers, no questions about the other home, no criticism of the other parent in earshot.

cards.title: What is worth matching
cards.body: Core routines such as bedtime, screens, homework and safety are the better-supported place to line up. Evidence that matching whole styles matters is mixed, and low conflict matters more.

cards.title: After you lost your temper
cards.body: Calm yourself first, go back and name it, say it was yours, then reconnect. Mistakes happen. A mistake does not make anyone bad.

cards.title: When siblings fight
cards.body: Step in only if someone could be hurt. Name each feeling, ask what they could try, then notice the fix. Common practice, but no sibling-specific trials were found.

out.headline: Warm, with clear limits.
out.prompt: Notice: what made that possible today?

out.headline: Firm today, with less warmth.
out.prompt: Notice: what was going on for you? One small warm moment can change the day.

out.headline: Warm today, with looser limits.
out.prompt: Notice: was it a choice, or were you tired? One clear limit may be enough.

out.headline: Low on both today.
out.prompt: Notice: are you okay? Support is fine to ask for. Tomorrow is a fresh day.

messages.text: You always let her stay up and it is your fault.

on.hint: Try the one thing that happened: "On Friday bedtime was late."
Describe the effect, not who is at fault.
Leave out the insult. It makes the real point harder to hear.

messages.text: Tell your dad he owes me.

on.hint: Send this to the other guardian directly. Please keep the child out of it.

messages.text: Ask Mia what Dad said about me.

on.hint: Please do not question the child about the other home.
Say what you need and by when, without a threat.
